session.inputs: data/notes.md@<commit>; calibrator/raw.toon@<commit>; public repositories; news retrieved 2026-10-02

questions.proposition: Will spending two hours this week prototyping the smallest proof-agent experiment be higher-value than reading two more papers on it?
questions.context: A recent open-source release makes small theorem-proving agents cheap to run locally.
questions.resolution_rule: Resolved true if a later note or repository shows the prototype ran and was judged more useful than the reading.

questions.proposition: Should I stop project X before investing another ten hours in it?
questions.context: The last three notes on X record no measurable progress.
questions.high_action: stop X and write down why
questions.low_action: continue X for ten more hours
questions.resolution_rule: Resolved true if X is stopped within the horizon and no later note regrets it.

questions.proposition: Am I continuing the site refactor because of sunk cost rather than expected future value?
questions.context: Repository activity shows refactor commits but no new readers' features in a month.
questions.resolution_rule: Unresolvable automatically unless a later note states the reason explicitly.

questions.proposition: Will the result I rated 80% last session still look right after this month's new evidence?
questions.context: Two later notes partly contradict it.
questions.resolution_rule: Resolved by the next session's answer to the same latent variable.

questions.proposition: Is a small immediate experiment better than more reading whenever my uncertainty is mainly empirical?
questions.resolution_rule: Unresolved until several later records show experiments outperforming reading, or not.

sources.title: Example release notes for a small proof agent

claims.claim: The release runs on a laptop GPU in under an hour per problem.
A note lists proof agents as a current interest, tagged #agents.
Three consecutive notes on X report no measurable progress.
Twelve of the last fifteen commits are refactors.
Four earlier answers favoured experiments when uncertainty was empirical.
